the minimum cardinality τ(H) of a set S of vertices intersecting all members of a given family H of subgraphs of a tree G is at most 2d2 times the maximum number v(H) of pairwise disjoint members of H, where d is the maximum number of connected components of a member of H. The result is generalized to graphs with bounded tree-width.

the maximum size of a collection of subforests of a graph with a bounded tree-width is bounded above by the minimum number of vertices that intersect all subforests, and that the minimum number of such vertices is bounded below by a function of the size of the collection.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of finding the minimum number of vertices of a graph that intersects every subgraph with at most d components.
the problem of determining a set of vertices that intersects all members in a family H of subgraphs.

the following problems: Given a graph H, what is the maximum number of copies of H in a given graph G? What is the minimum number of vertices in G which intersects all the copies of H? What is the maximum number and minimum number of edges in G intersecting all the copies of a graph H?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

if G is a tree with n vertices, and H is a collection of subgraph of G, then the minimum cardinality τ(H) of a vertex cover of H is bounded above by 2n2v(H) if each member of H has at most two connected components, and is bounded above by n2v(H) otherwise.
for any hypergraph H of subgraphs of a graph G, τ(H) ≤ (2d2 + d)v(H), where d is the maximum number of vertices of a member of H.

for every graph G and every set H of subgraphs of bounded degree and tree-width, there exists a set of vertices V of G of cardinality at most 2d2 times the maximum number of disjoint subgraphs of H, such that every subgraph of H contains a vertex of V.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the minimum number of vertices that cover a collection of graphs with bounded number of connected components is bounded by a polynomial function of the maximum number of graphs that share no vertex.

, if H is a collection of subgraph of a graph G, and v(H) is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint members of H, then the minimum cardinality τ(H) of a set of vertex that intersects all members H is bounded above by a constant depending only on the maximum degree d of G and the tree-width of G.
, if a graph G is a tree, then τ(H) ≤ (2d2 − 2d) v(H) + 2d, and if G has a bounded tree width, then τ(H)/v(H) ≤ O(d2) and the constant of proportionality can be taken to be 2d2 − d − 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the covering number of a hypergraph of trees is at most quadratic in the size of a maximum antichain.
, when H is a hypergraph of bounded size, then the covering number τ(H) of H is not very much larger than v(H), the vertex cover number of H.
the covering number of a hypergraph of trees can be bounded by a function of the size of the largest tree in the hypergraph.
